sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:1
items.html:
Explains: the restriction and the screen. And there are four matters in it: 1. The restriction was in one equivalence from all sides. 2. The matter of the screen: since every drawing of light is in Phase 4, a restraining force is needed so that the light will not extend also into Phase 4, and this force is called a screen. 3. Two phases in Malchut: 1. that she is restricted from receiving light into herself of her own will, and this applies in the circles. 2. that she is restricted by a restraining force upon her, namely a screen, and this applies in the Sefirot of straightness. 4. The upper light is in absolute rest, and does not cease shining even for a moment. And whenever the emanated being yearns, he draws the light to himself.

The difference between restriction and screen.
And now that we already know well the four degrees in the will to receive, each one lower than the other, in their exact measure, let us now explain the matter of the restriction and the screen, and the difference between them. And behold, the restriction has already been explained well in Part 1, and also here in the Inner Light, and there is no need to repeat the matter. And the main thing we need for our purpose is the matter of the equivalence that existed there (see above in the Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 90, beginning "the restriction" and "circle," see there well).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:2
items.html:
The four phases received in the restriction the matter of cause and effect.
And it has been explained there, that since the light of Ein Sof is equal in absolute equivalence, it was also compelled to restrict itself in one equivalence from all the phases, meaning, that all four phases that were restricted are equal in one level, without the distinction of refinement and coarseness that makes four degrees, each lower than the other, down to Phase 4, the coarsest and lowest of them all, but rather they are in one equivalence. And all that was added in the restriction, to be discerned in it more than in Ein Sof, blessed be He, is only the matter of the four phases, from the aspect that they are caused and unfold one from another, in the manner of cause and effect: that Phase 1 is the cause and reason for the revelation of Phase 2, and Phase 2 is the cause of Phase 3, and Phase 3 is the cause of Phase 4, except that they are in one equivalence from the aspect of refinement and level, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:3
items.html:
The cause and effect that exists in the four phases did not exist in Ein Sof.
And this matter of cause and effect, which in any event divides them into four phases, was not revealed in Ein Sof, blessed be He, before the restriction, for there, not even the phase of the vessel as a whole was discernible, but everything was entirely light, as written in Part 1, but rather, after the light of Ein Sof departed from those phases, these phases were then discerned and the matter was revealed, that now there is to discern: the light by itself, meaning, that which was in them before the restriction, and the four phases by themselves, remained empty of light, for after the restriction it was revealed, that these phases are not one thing with the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, as it appeared before the restriction. And this is like the example of a candle included within a torch, which is not discernible, and when it is separated from the torch, it is then discernible to all, and understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:4
items.html: And at first glance, one may ask: since the essence of the restriction was only in Phase 4, it is revealed that that phase is not fit for receiving the light, whereas the first three phases, upon which the restriction did not take place, it is revealed that they are fit for receiving the light, and thus we would arrive at a distinction of superiority and importance of one over the other, meaning, that Phase 4 is lower than the first three phases.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:5
items.html:
The restriction was not due to any inferiority of Phase 4, but only for the sake of adornment.
However, the matter is, that the restriction of the light from Phase 4 was not due to any inferiority in it, God forbid, for we are still dealing with the Malchut of Ein Sof, blessed be He, where Phase 4 was, in the phase of the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, itself, and how is it even possible to entertain the thought, that the restriction was due to an inferiority of Phase 4, but rather the restriction was for the sake of adornment alone, for this Malchut desired the phase of adhesion, in the utmost possible elevation, to cleave entirely to the Emanator, which is the matter of the greatest equivalence of form to the Emanator (as written above in the Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, Item 90, beginning "the restriction," see there), and therefore the level of Phase 4 did not fall, even after the restriction.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:6
items.html:
The drawing of the line was first in Phase 4, and therefore a restraining force was needed over Phase 4, so that the light would not enter it.
Now let us explain the matter of the screen that was made over Phase 4, which is Malchut, for at the time of the world of restriction, meaning, the Malchut of Ein Sof, blessed be He, that was clothed there, as is known, that every degree begins from the Malchut of its Upper One, which becomes its first substance (as above, Item 27), and behold, when this restricted Malchut returned and drew the upper light for the three phases alone, this drawing was necessarily accompanied by the yearning that was in the Phase 4 within her, for the first three phases are not at all vessels of receiving and drawing. Therefore it was necessary that she draw the upper light at first to all four phases, meaning, even to her Phase 4, except that in order that the light not reach Phase 4, she was compelled to add a new force, to restrain the light from extending into Phase 4.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:7
items.html:
The restraining force that was added over Phase 4 is called a screen.
And this new force that she added is called by the name "screen," and this screen is the root cause in the matter of the drawing of the light of the line over the three phases: for the restriction that she made, meaning, that she removed her will to receive in Phase 4, was sufficient only for the departure of the upper light from her alone, however, afterward, when she returned and drew the light, she was compelled to arouse her Phase 4 again, in order to draw the new drawing, and thus, had she not made a new force with respect to the extension of the light, the light would again have reached Phase 4 as well. Thus, the main cause for the drawing of the light of the line over the three phases is only the force of the "screen," which she made anew with respect to the light. And understand well these two phases, namely the restriction and the screen, which are the foundations for the entire continuation of this wisdom.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:8
items.html:
The restriction was of her own knowledge. The screen pushes back the light by a controlling force not of her own knowledge.
And understand the difference between the matter of the restriction that the Malchut of Ein Sof made, which is the phase of the departure from the magnitude of the will to receive, of her own will and choice, for the sake of the greatest equivalence of form with the Emanator, and the matter of the screen, which is the phase of the restraining force, in control and compulsion, so that the light will not reach Phase 4.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:9
items.html: And the reason for the matter is, that even though both the restriction and the screen were made by the Malchut of Ein Sof, blessed be He, as above, nevertheless you already know, that when the spiritual acquires a new form, added to its own form, it is thereby discerned as two spiritual entities, and as two phases, distant from one another according to the measure of the magnitude of the change of form that exists between these two forms. For just as physical things are separated from one another by an axe, and are distanced from one another by place and area, so spiritual things are distinguished from one another by a renewal of form, and are distanced from one another according to the measure of the magnitude of the change found between one form and another, whether less or more.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:10
items.html:
The screen is an offshoot of the restricted Malchut. What is a will in the upper becomes a force in the lower.
Therefore, after the aforementioned Malchut made a drawing for the light of the line over the three phases, this drawing is discerned as a new form, added to the form of the restriction. In such a way, that there are now two phases in the aforesaid Malchut: the first is the restricted Malchut, which is the first form that was made in the Malchut of Ein Sof, blessed be He, and received the new form called "restricted Malchut." And afterward, when this Malchut made a drawing after the light of the three phases, a new form was born and came forth, called "screen," with respect to the light, so that it not appear in her in Phase 4. And it is known that every will that exists in the upper becomes a controlling force in the branch that comes forth from it, and since the screen is a branch and offshoot of the restricted Malchut, therefore, even though Malchut restricted herself of her own will and knowledge, without any control by the one above her, nevertheless, the offshoot that is drawn from her, namely the screen, is already ridden upon by the restriction in absolute control, it being a second degree to the world of restriction, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:11
items.html:
The difference between circles and straightness is in the screen that was renewed in the ten Sefirot of straightness.
What is explained from the above is, that there are two phases of Malchut: the first is "restricted Malchut," and the second is Malchut that has a screen in her. And know, that this is the entire difference between the Sefirot of circles and the Sefirot of straightness, which are called the line. For in the ten Sefirot of circles, the Malchut in them is from the phase of the restricted Malchut, where there is no screen, as above, whereas in the ten Sefirot of straightness, the Malchut in them is corrected with the aforesaid screen. As will be written below.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:12
items.html:
The reason that the light strikes and wishes to enter Phase 4 is that the emanated being drew it so.
Now you will understand well the matter of the reflected light, that rises through the coupling by striking, from the meeting of the upper light with the screen upon Phase 4, which we began to explain above (Item 18, beginning "and the matter"). And you will understand what we said there, that the upper light is not particular about the restriction that the emanated being made, and it descends to extend also into Phase 4, see there. The reason is, that the emanated being himself necessarily draws it so from the outset, for it has already been explained (above, Part 1, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 2) that the upper light is always in a state of absolute rest, and does not cease shining upon the lower ones even for a moment, for it does not fall, God forbid, under happenstance and renewal, and all the matters of the extension of the upper light mentioned are meant with regard to the drawing on the part of the emanated being, who receives from the upper light, according to the preparation of the will to receive, meaning, the yearning within him, as has been explained above (Part 2, Item 50, beginning "and behold").

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:13
items.html:
The drawing of the emanated being is what we refer to as the extension of the upper light.
And at the very moment that the emanated being yearns to receive from the upper light, he immediately draws the upper light to himself, similar to lighting a candle from a candle, in which the first is not diminished; so too, when the emanated being draws the upper light to himself, the upper light is not diminished at all on account of that portion which the emanated being drew into himself, and it likewise has no impression or extension whatsoever on account of the drawing of the emanated being, but rather, only in order to accustom the ear, we refer to the drawing of the emanated being by the name "extension of the upper light." And remember this in all places, for we always speak in the language of the extension of the upper light, but the intention is with regard to the drawing of the emanated being himself, upon his own yearning alone.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 5:14
items.html:
The portion of light that was to enter Phase 4, and was pushed back from her, becomes the reflected light.
Therefore, after the restriction, when the Malchut of Ein Sof, blessed be He, returned and drew the upper light, since she drew it through the yearning that was in her Phase 4, as above, the upper light was thus drawn also to her Phase 4, but on account of the screen that she made, to restrain the light from extending into Phase 4, that portion of light returned backward, whereby she fulfilled her original will, that the light reach her only in three phases. However, that portion of the light, which the screen returned backward to its root, meaning, the portion fit for Phase 4, was not lost to her, but became a great light, clothing the three phases of the upper light, from the place of the screen and upward to the root, so that this reflected light became a vessel of receiving for the three phases of the upper light, in the place of Phase 4, as above (Item 21, beginning "and now," see there).
